eval_feedback.overall: All 14 assertions pass on the literal text of features-backbone.md. Contamination risk: the actor-naming assertion ('Los actores... Visitor/Coach — NOT System...') and, to a lesser extent, the 'no actor prefix'/'no conjunction'/'no technical terms in names' formatting assertions are exactly the kind of surface-level, literally-quotable checks the executor could satisfy simply by having read the answer key rather than by genuine skill-driven reasoning — the executor admitted this for the actor-naming decision specifically. By contrast, the System Task classification assertions (the workflow-transition test correctly keeping auto-dismiss standalone while embedding hover-pause/manual-dismiss/session-gating/threshold-gating as preconditions instead of System Tasks) show real methodological work: the Discovery Context and body text lay out multi-step reasoning (distinguishing autonomous timeout from indivisible user-response, and distinguishing a display precondition from a workflow transition) that goes well beyond restating assertion text, and would be much harder to fake by pattern-matching the eval file alone. The PRD-traceability and coverage-of-key-capabilities assertions likewise required actually parsing the PRD's FR/US sections rather than the eval file, so those are also more likely genuine.
